title: Momotarou Mystery Solving Tour
notes: Detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ayumi, Mitsuhiko, Genta, Professor Agasa) omitted by convention; they solve the codes but are not suspects/victims/witnesses to the crime itself. case_type: murder. DISCREPANCY vs old cases/ file: the old file's e1 event ('Momoi is involved in a road accident death he never tells anyone about, confessing it only in a sealed time capsule memo') conflates two separate people/facts. The transcript is clear these are distinct: (1) Shunya, a sixth classmate/play-director, died in a real car accident 15 years ago -- unrelated to Momoi causing anyone's death, and its 'ordinariness' is only vaguely doubted by Momoi in a closing monologue, never investigated on-screen or resolved as a second crime; (2) Momoi's own sealed time-capsule confession was about being bullied into committing a robbery/theft as a child (a crime against property, not a death), which Shunya witnessed and tried to shield him from. Momoi's real motive for killing Inui Seiko was fear that unburying the capsules for her 'research' would expose that old confession and derail his election candidacy and engagement -- not fear of a death being exposed. This file corrects that. Also corrected: the old file lists only 4 suspects and omits Shunya (backstory figure central to motive and to the closing scene) and Kijima Yayoi (present throughout, functions as Momoi's alibi witness, not merely a suspect). The old file's single clue (mirror dying-message reading) is kept but paired with a second real comparative clue the old file missed entirely: the half-a-ticket-stamp match between the museum pamphlet left with the victim's body and the banknote found in Momoi's wallet, which is what actually pins the theft-from-the-corpse (frame-up attempt against Onitsura) on him.

clues.desc: Dying message read left-to-right spells ONI (demon), but the victim was left-handed and her finger position shows she wrote right-to-left, backward -- the true message is MOMO, naming Momoi, not Onitsura or Saruwatari.

A half ticket-stamp on the back of the victim's museum pamphlet matches the other half on a banknote found in Momoi's wallet -- the two were stamped together while overlapping, proving the bill came from the victim's wallet.
